rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for the physical container.

example.english: We keep a bucket by the door for washing the floor.
example.traditional: 門口擺咗個水桶，方便洗地。
example.jyutping: mun4 hau2 baai2 zo2 go3 seoi2 tung2 fong1 bin6 sai2 dei6

rows.note: Use this for a large amount of liquid or other things rather than for the container itself.

example.english: There’s loads of ice in the fridge—enough to fill a bucket and make lots of cold drinks.
example.traditional: 雪櫃入面大把冰，夠整好多杯凍飲喇。
example.jyutping: syut3 gwai6 jap6 min6 daai6 baa2 bing1 gau3 zing2 hou2 do1 bui1 dung3 jam2 laa3

rows.note: Use this when “a bucket” means the amount that one bucket holds.

example.english: One bucket of water is enough to wash the car.
example.jyutping: sai2 ce1 jat1 tung2 seoi2 zau6 gau3 laa3

rows.note: Use this in basketball when “bucket” means a successful field goal or score.

example.english: That last bucket helped us come from behind and win.
example.traditional: 最後嗰個入球，幫我哋反勝㗎。
example.jyutping: zeoi3 hau6 go2 go3 jap6 kau4 bong1 ngo5 dei6 faan2 sing3 gaa3
